articles.title: Democrats investigating sexual harassment allegation against incoming Ohio congressman
articles.summary: An aide claims incoming congressman Brian Poindexter made sexually harassing comments during his campaign.
articles.body:
House Democrats are investigating an aide's complaint that newly elected congressman Brian Poindexter made sexually harassing comments toward her during his campaign.

The investigation is being led by an independent firm hired by the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC), the group confirmed in a statement to CNN.

Poindexter defeated Rep. Max Miller, a former Trump adviser whose ex-wife accused him of domestic violence, which he has denied. The unwelcome development comes as Democrats are trying to focus on building out their agenda on the heels of a massive victory in November.

"The DCCC has been made aware of the allegations and takes them seriously," said Julie Merz, executive director of the campaign group.

In a statement, a spokesperson for Poindexter's campaign said: "Brian gave what he thought was an innocuous compliment to a volunteer. He heard later that it made her feel uncomfortable and he felt awful."

The spokesperson added, "When Brian learned about this, we immediately began to work to get to the bottom of it with an outside HR firm. Neither Brian nor the campaign ever wants anyone to feel uncomfortable."

The Democrats' campaign arm was alerted about the allegation just before the election by the Blue Dog PAC and the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC, the groups said in a statement to CNN. Both groups pulled their endorsement of Poindexter until DCCC finishes its investigation.

"The individual requested that we did not disclose any details about this publicly because she did not want her identity becoming public and she wanted an opportunity to determine how she wanted to proceed while protecting herself," said the statement from both groups. "We respected her desires, and also felt we needed to immediately pull our endorsements pending the investigation being completed. The investigation is ongoing and we await the results."

Poindexter's removal from the two group's endorsement lists came as members were arriving at the Capitol for new member orientation. Sources familiar with the matter told CNN that Poindexter was not invited to the new member orientations for the Progressive Caucus or the Blue Dog Coalition.

Cheyenne Hunt, whose group Reckoning Action is providing support to the anonymous woman, told CNN she was contacted by the aide two days before Poindexter flipped Ohio's 7th District. Hunt described her as a "very low-level staffer" but did not provide additional details in order to protect her anonymity. Hunt declined to discuss the specifics of her allegation.

Lawmakers are in ongoing discussions about how to improve Capitol Hill's handling of sexual harassment claims, following a spate of complaints about other politicians earlier this year. A group of Democrats are pushing for stricter regulations around conduct as part of a rules package for the full House for next year.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has been made aware of the allegation about Poindexter, according to a person familiar with the discussions. His office referred CNN to the campaign arm, pending the ongoing investigation.

Poindexter ran on an economic populist message and played up his background as a union ironworker, but he also leaned into his role as a father. In one early ad, he appeared with his daughters as they ribbed him.

On the campaign trail, Poindexter's history also became a focal point of Miller's attacks against him including a 2013 fight with another man at a baseball game, where he was arrested, and a 1998 incident in which he was arrested by police when they suspected he was in possession of crack cocaine.

Poindexter was never charged in either incident and told CNN in an interview in October he never used hard drugs in his life. He also said he is routinely drug tested for his job and has never failed a test.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com
authors: Allison Gordon, Lauren Fox, Sarah Ferris, CNN

articles.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
articles.summary: Georgia GOP Gov. Brian Kemp is also said to be getting encouragement to run.
articles.body:
Supporters and donors have been encouraging Republican Arkansas governor and former White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, according to multiple sources with direct knowledge of the situation.

​When asked about the outreach Sanders has been receiving, her communications director Sam Dubke told ABC News that "Governor Sanders looks forward to serving the people of Arkansas for the next four years."

​Sanders, the daughter of Mike Huckabee, himself a former Arkansas governor, Repubican presidential candidate and current U.S. ambassador to Israel, won re-election as governor last week. She became the first woman ever elected Arkansas governor in 2022.

Before becoming governor, Sanders served as President Donald Trump's press secretary in his first term from July 2017 to June 2019 after having served as deputy press secretary. She was also a senior adviser to Trump's 2016 presidential campaign.

​While Sanders formally briefed the White House press corps less than her predecessors, she became one of Trump's closest and most trusted advisers and has maintained a close relationship with him, having worked for Trump in the White House for 3 1/2 years .

Sanders has long been viewed as a rising star in the Republican Party.

In 2023, a few months after winning the gubernatorial race in Arkansas, Sanders delivered the Republican response to former President Joe Biden's State of the Union address -- remarks usually reserved for individuals seen as on their way up in the party.

Georgia's retiring popular two-term Republican Gov. Brian Kemp is also considering a presidential bid after he leaves office in January and has been encouraged by donors and other Republican officials to run, a source familiar with his thinking told ABC News.

​In the days leading up to the midterm elections, Kemp traveled to South Carolina, one of the early nominating states for Republicans, to campaign for Gov.-elect Alan Wilson.

ABC News has reached out to Kemp's political operation for comment.

​After Republicans' midterm losses, the party is reflecting on what went wrong and how to move forward, with some of those conversations happening publicly.

​Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, who has not ruled out a 2028 presidential run, called Republicans' performance in the midterm elections a " Watergate-level repudiation" of the party.

​Outgoing Florida Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis described the election results as a "meteor strike," arguing that even a "wave" fails to capture the scale of the Republican losses.

​DeSantis is keeping his options open for another presidential run, two people familiar with his thinking told ABC News, after the governor said Florida fended off a blue wave in this year's midterm elections.

articles.title: Carne suína brasileira: Ministro negocia fim de veto nas Filipinas | G1
articles.standfirst: André de Paula (Agricultura) disse que tem feito reuniões com autoridades filipinas e que suspensão da importação não deve continuar em 2027, um receio dos produtores brasileiros.
articles.summary: Carne suína brasileira: André de Paula negocia nas Filipinas para assegurar que a suspensão das vendas seja de apenas 60 dias e não prejudique o setor em 2027.
articles.body:
O ministro da Agricultura e Pecuária, André de Paula, afirmou neste sábado (14) que está "otimista" com as negociações do governo brasileiro com autoridades das Filipinas em relação à importação pelo país asiático da carne suína brasileira.

🔎Nesta semana, o governo das Filipinas suspendeu as importações de carne suína . O mercado filipino é o maior comprador da carne suína do Brasil, com 25% do total exportado pelo país. Quase metade da carne suína consumida nas Filipinas é de origem brasileira ( leia mais aqui ).

Em entrevista a jornalistas em Manila, capital das Filipinas, André de Paula afirmou que terá uma reunião com o secretário de Agricultura do país asiático na próxima segunda-feira (16) para tratar do tema.

O ministro destacou que a suspensão da compra da carne suína do Brasil é "uma medida de 60 dias" e, portanto, não deve se estender ao longo de 2027. Esse é um dos receios do governo e de produtores brasileiros.

"Iniciamos uma conversa com os presidentes e ministros. Eu estou muito otimista que nós possamos avançar. Acho que esse balanço será possível na segunda-feira, quando estarei aqui, com a equipe técnica do Ministério, vamos nos reunir com o secretário de Agricultura [das Filipinas] e com a sua equipe técnica", declarou André de Paula.

"Isso vai nos dar oportunidade de conhecer com mais detalhes, mas o que poderia dizer neste momento é que os sinais são positivos, são tranquilizadores e estou muito otimista. Posso afirmar, isso foi colocado pelo próprio presidente, essa é uma medida de 60 dias", completou.

O ministro da Agricultura disse ainda que o governo brasileiro está disposto a aceitar pleitos do governo filipino na área e disse que os dois países têm uma relação "muito boa", "sólida" e de 80 anos.

O governo filipino disse que a decisão de restringir as importações foi tomada para proteger os produtores locais, que aumentaram a produção e pressionam para recuperar o mercado perdido para países com preço mais competitivo, como o Brasil.

A medida afeta todos os países que vendem nove categorias de produtos suínos para as Filipinas – como carnes frescas, congeladas e miúdos

De janeiro a outubro de 2026, o Brasil vendeu mais de 300 mil toneladas em produtos do gênero para o país, negócio de mais de US$ 587 milhões.

O ministro da Agricultura, André de Paula, concede entrevista em Manila, nas Filipinas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Lula nas Filipinas: parceria em semicondutores e minerais críticos | G1
articles.standfirst: País asiático tem desenvolvido indústria de chips enquanto Brasil possui a segunda maior reserva de terras raras do mundo. Lula fez postagem nas redes sociais sobre visita a Manila.
articles.summary: Lula e o presidente Ferdinand Marcos Jr. discutem a integração entre as reservas de minerais críticos do Brasil e a indústria de semicondutores das Filipinas.
articles.body:
Lula se encontra com o presidente das Filipinas, Ferdinand Marcos Jr, em Manila — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/Presidência da República

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) afirmou neste sábado (14) que o Brasil e as Filipinas têm potencial para integrar cadeias produtivas nas áreas de minerais críticos, semicondutores e microeletrônica.

A declaração foi feita em uma publicação nas redes sociais durante visita oficial a Manila , capital do país asiático, onde o petista se encontrou com o presidente filipino Ferdinand Marcos Jr .

Segundo Lula , a ideia é aproximar centros de pesquisa, universidades e empresas dos países na área. O Brasil detém a segunda maior reserva global de terras raras . Já as Filipinas possuem um parque industrial voltado à montagem e produção de chips e componentes eletrônicos .

"Na área de ciência e tecnologia, vamos aproximar centros de pesquisa, universidades e empresas inovadoras dos dois países. Como polos regionais de inovação, Brasil e Filipinas têm muito a ganhar com a integração de cadeias de minerais críticos, semicondutores e microeletrônica", disse o presidente após o encontro com Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

🔋Os minerais críticos, como lítio, níquel, cobalto, cobre e elementos de terras raras, são matérias-primas essenciais para fabricar baterias, equipamentos de energia limpa e componentes eletrônicos avançados. Os semicondutores, utilizados em celulares, computadores, carros e equipamentos militares, dependem diretamente desses insumos processados.

Entre os ministros que acompanham Lula na viagem a Manila, estão Alexandre Silveira (Minas e Energia), Márcio Elias Rosa (Desenvolvimento, Indústria e Comércio), Mauro Vieira (Relações Exteriores) e André de Paula (Agricultura e Pecuária).

No X, Lula destacou que esta é a primeira visita de um presidente brasileiro ao país asiático, com o qual o Brasil celebra 80 anos de relações diplomáticas.

Nas Filipinas, o petista participa da Cúpula da Associação de Nações do Sudeste Asiático (ASEAN). Também está prevista a participação do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , no evento.

O mercado filipino é o maior comprador da carne de porco do Brasil, com 25% do total exportado pelo país. Quase metade da carne suína consumida nas Filipinas é de origem brasileira.

Na viagem ao país asiático, a comitiva brasileira deve tratar do tema. A principal preocupação é evitar que a restrição de importações se estenda por 2027 .

Lula foi recebido com uma apresentaçã na chegada à Base Aérea Villamor, em Manila, capital das Filipinas — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/Presidência da República

articles.title: Silicon Valley plots Jensen Huang’s comeback
articles.summary: The tech industry is already thinking of ways the ousted Nvidia chief could return to a seat in power.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — A day after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, Silicon Valley is already anticipating his comeback.

As a close ally of Donald Trump, regularly taking calls — even publicly — from the president, Huang became one of the most prominent and influential voices in Washington for the largely California-based tech industry, leaving a vacuum with his departure from one of the world's most profitable companies that has become the backbone of the AI boom.

But while national security hawks and tech skeptics in Washington prepare to haul him before Congress to bring further scrutiny of his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, Silicon Valley leaders are mourning his swift exit and positing ways that he could return.

The founder of defense tech giant Anduril, Palmer Luckey , and Perplexity AI CEO Aravind Srinivas have rushed to Huang's defense, while SpaceXSI CEO Elon Musk has even floated the idea of hiring him.

Five other tech industry insiders also told POLITICO they expect Huang to eventually return in a major way to leadership within Silicon Valley. Another three were not quite as confident, but indicated they wouldn't be surprised if it happened.

"It is inevitable, with all of the value that he's created and his role commonly accepted as the godfather of AI, that he will have a second act," said an executive at a prominent California startup who was granted anonymity to frankly discuss industry dynamics. "And that any number of hyperscalers and startups are tripping over themselves to reach out to him and bring him on, regardless of any transgressions."

Despite losing his lofty perch at Nvidia, Huang still has a net worth of roughly $145 billion , an ecosystem of connections in high places and a sterling entrepreneurial reputation within the industry, some noted.

"That kind of influence doesn't just disappear overnight," said Joseph Hoefer, chief AI officer at the lobbying firm Monument Advocacy. "I wouldn't confuse losing his position with losing his ability to shape what comes down the road."

A spokesperson for Huang did not respond to a request for comment on his future plans.

Three of the people who spoke with POLITICO said it would be easier for Huang to start a new venture using his wealth of capital, rather than joining an already established company.

The connection to allegations of espionage "would make it much harder for any public company to bring him on board in a leadership role," said Scott Gerber, partner at the tech strategy consultancy Vrge.

Others have started to seize on questions about the initial reports of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, potentially undercutting any support for his ouster. Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), who will likely be the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, told POLITICO this week that he's unsure whether Huang's paramour was knowingly providing information to China based on briefings from U.S. intelligence officials.

David Sacks, Trump's former AI czar and a venture capitalist prominent on the tech right, highlighted reports that some in the U.S. intel community have similar doubts. "The spy narrative is collapsing already," he wrote in an X post .

Recouping influence in Washington, however, may still be trickier than in Silicon Valley. Huang has been a commanding voice in advocating for looser restrictions on exports to China of advanced semiconductors — necessary for the development of artificial intelligence. That position is being called into question by lawmakers in Congress, given an initial Financial Times report that U.S. intelligence believed Huang was having an affair with a spy.

"His standing in industry might be recoverable over time," said Philip Reiner, CEO of the Institute for Security and Technology think tank in California and a former senior director at the National Security Council. "Rebuilding credibility in Washington on China policy is extremely challenging."

Even still, much of the cachet he built was specifically connected to Trump's White House, meaning it would have an expiration date regardless, ahead of the 2028 election, others noted.

"[M]uch of his political influence was tied to his relationship with the current administration, and that kind of access will be hard to rebuild once the political landscape shifts," said Nu Wexler, a principal at Four Corners Public Affairs who advises tech companies on policy communications.

This delicate position raises the stakes for an upcoming House hearing on the scandal, for which Huang has agreed to testify .

"If he can come before Congress and own mistakes, but also explain them and still be a credible voice, that will go a long way towards opening the door for anything else that he would want to do in Washington and the private sector," said Daniel Castro, president of the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation — a think tank funded by Big Tech companies like Amazon and Microsoft.

images.caption: Silicon Valley plots Jensen Huang’s comeback

articles.title: Kreiss-Tomkins becomes first Democrat since 1998 elected governor in Alaska
articles.summary: JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — Alaska voters have elected a Democrat for governor for the first time since 1998, part of a national midterm elections wave that gave t...
articles.body:
JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — Alaska voters have elected a Democrat for governor for the first time since 1998, part of a national midterm elections wave that gave the party sweeping wins in state governments across the country.

Former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans, including one endorsed by President Donald Trump. His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.

Kreiss-Tomkins, often referred to as JKT, completed a political comeback three years after leaving the state House. He traveled throughout Alaska to build his coalition and focused on affordability, advocated for full funding of public schools and called for all oil and gas producers to pay corporate income tax. He also sought a moratorium on new data centers until state lawmakers pass regulations for their development.

He said Alaska had become "broken" under eight years of outgoing Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy and needed a change. He cited among other issues a state ferry system that he said has been left in shambles, with routes to many communities cut drastically. The ferry is a key mode of transportation for southeast Alaska communities not connected by roads, some of which also have limited air service.

Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, emphasized a willingness to work across party lines and said he wanted a Cabinet with Republicans, Democrats and independents.

"If they're competent, if they're service-minded, if they're entrepreneurial, if they're problem-solvers, you're on the team. Game on," he said during a candidate forum last month. "Let's go, and let's get Alaska back on track."

Republican U.S. Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who has at times been at odds with her party, including Trump, endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins a week before the election. She said Kreiss-Tomkins "understands that governing requires listening to people with different perspectives and finding common ground to solve the problems all of us face."

Three former governors including Democrat Tony Knowles, independent Bill Walker and Republican Frank Murkowski, the senator's father, also endorsed him.

In a statement declaring victory earlier Friday, Kreiss-Tomkins said voters wanted change and "a government that works across party lines to move Alaska forward. Our administration will not waste a single day getting to work to solve problems for Alaska." He said his campaign had more than 10,000 donors.

His campaign did not immediately respond to requests for comment after The Associated Press called the race.

He defeated Republicans Bernadette Wilson, Dave Bronson and Treg Taylor. Trump had endorsed Wilson, a business owner, and criticized the other Republican candidates for staying in the race. Bronson is a former mayor of Anchorage, Alaska's largest city, while Taylor was a state attorney general under Dunleavy.

Bronson congratulated Kreiss-Tomkins on social media and wished him success. A message seeking comment from Wilson's campaign was not immediately returned.

Many Republicans saw ranking as their party's best shot of retaining the governor's seat. It was a message that conflicted with that of Trump, who has consistently complained about Alaska's unusual voting method, including during a rally in Alaska in October.

Kreiss-Tomkins finished first in August's open primary, followed by a second Democrat, Tom Begich, who withdrew from the race. Begich's campaign at the time said it had concluded that the "strongest path to victory is to bring Democratic voters, donors and resources together behind one candidate." Wilson finished third in the primary.

Kreiss-Tomkins said compromise "is a virtue, not a dirty word," and said he saw the mission of the new governor as working with lawmakers to resolve longstanding problems in the state.

The state's last Democratic governor, Tony Knowles, left office in 2002 after serving back-to-back terms. Walker served from 2014 to 2018.

Kreiss-Tomkins will be sworn in Dec. 7. His lieutenant governor is Zac Johnson, an independent.
